headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend intact, but leverage cooled and ETF flows dipped

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early-stage uptrend with medium confidence (69/100), and the one-month momentum picture is now strong. That supports a measured increase in acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, while holding part of the budget in reserve: only half of recent days closed above the long-term average, that average is still declining, ETF buying paused at the end of September, and long-term interest rates are high. This is a budget-posture view built on past data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is 19% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.19).
90-day return +34%; 50-day average 9.5% above the 200-day; momentum score +0.46.
Funding back below normal (z -0.68) despite Fear & Greed at 72.
200-day average still falling (-4.6% over 90 days); breadth only 50%.
watch: The tension today is between momentum and short-term positioning. Momentum just crossed into strongly bullish territory (+0.46) on a +34% 90-day move, yet sentiment fell from +0.445 to +0.11 in one day as funding swung from +0.79 to -0.68, the long/short ratio dropped toward balance at 1.04, and spot ETFs posted about $148.7M of outflows on 30 September, ending a nine-day inflow streak. That means the trailing price trend is running ahead of fresh leveraged and ETF demand, with breadth still only at 50% and the 200-day average still sloping down. A return to ETF inflows and breadth moving clearly above 50% would confirm the read; several sessions of outflows, or price slipping back toward the roughly $73,700 short-term-holder cost basis, would weaken it.
analysis: Short-term sentiment is neutral (+0.11 of a possible ±1), a sharp step down from yesterday's +0.445, which was just shy of strongly bullish. The main driver of that drop is funding: the z-score swung back from +0.79 to -0.68 in a day, so leveraged longs are no longer paying an above-normal premium, which cuts against the still-warm Fear & Greed reading of 72 (Greed) and leaves mood and positioning disagreeing again. Positioning data points the same way as funding rather than the greed reading: the long/short ratio eased from 1.35 to 1.04, close to balanced, even as open interest rose to about $8.22B from roughly $7.98B, a mix that suggests new positions are not one-sidedly long. Bitcoin.com reported that market-wide liquidations on 1 October were about $193M, with bitcoin's share falling to around $35M from over $80M a day earlier, so the cooling came without a forced flush. Volatility is neutral for the lean, with realised volatility at the 50th percentile of its two-year range, Bollinger width at 17%, DVOL at 36.5 and the VIX at 16.4, while a stablecoin supply ratio of 5.4 indicates a moderate pool of sidelined stablecoin liquidity. The lean would move back toward bullish if funding turned positive again alongside the greed reading, and toward bearish if Fear & Greed dropped while open interest kept climbing on negative funding.

Medium-term momentum is strongly bullish (+0.46 of a possible ±1), crossing the +0.45 threshold today from +0.39 yesterday and now the strongest of the three dimensions. Reinforcing that, the 90-day rate of change is +34%, weekly RSI is 59.8 (firm but well short of overbought), and the 50-day average sits 9.5% above the 200-day, keeping the structure on the golden-cross side. Participation has also improved at the margin: 50% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average, up from 49% yesterday, though that is still only half and remains the weakest part of the momentum picture. Network and market-share data are supportive, with active addresses 11% above their yearly average (up from 5%) and BTC dominance at 58.6%, indicating activity concentrated in bitcoin rather than rotating into altcoins. The one clear item pulling against the lean is flows: spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $148.7M of net outflows on 30 September per Farside data, led by Fidelity's FBTC (-$125.6M), ending a nine-day inflow streak that had brought in roughly $3.08B. The next FOMC meeting is on 27–28 October, and the softer August PCE print reported on 30 September had already lowered priced odds of an October hike. The lean would strengthen if breadth moved clearly above 50% with ETF flows returning to inflows, and weaken if weekly RSI rolled over or outflows persisted for several sessions.

The long-term trend is bullish-leaning (+0.26 of a possible ±1), a modest improvement from +0.24 yesterday but still an early, not yet confirmed lean. Supporting it, price is about 19% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.19); cutting against it, that average is still falling, down 4.6% over 90 days, though the decline continues to flatten from -4.9% yesterday. That pattern of price reclaiming the trend line before the line itself turns up is why the trend score is positive but well below the momentum score. Valuation is neutral for the lean: the 200-week multiple of 1.28 is mid-range, price is 32% below its all-time high, the Puell Multiple of 1.08 puts miner revenue in a normal band, and the Pi-Cycle gap of -55% is far from the zone historically seen near cycle tops (context only, not scored). On-chain cost basis is supportive, with KuCoin News reporting the short-term-holder cost basis at about $73,700 as of 1 October, roughly 14% below price, meaning recent buyers are on average in profit. Macro remains the clearest cross-current: the US 10-year yield is 5.24% against a fed funds rate of 3.63%, a meaningful competing return for non-yielding assets, while structural holdings reinforce the lean, with cumulative spot ETF net inflows of about $57.5B and public companies holding roughly 1.28M BTC. The lean would strengthen if the 200-day slope turned positive, and would flip toward neutral or bearish if price fell back below that average or under the short-term-holder cost basis while long yields stayed this high.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels: the +34% 90-day move and a 50-day average 9.5% above the 200-day give campaigns a concrete recovery story to lead with. Keep messaging on the trend and the quarter just closed rather than urgency — leverage has cooled (funding z -0.68) and ETF flows dipped, so FOMO angles would run ahead of the data while Fear & Greed already sits at 72.
